If symptoms of buprenorphine toxicity or overdose occur and the concurrent CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, the patient should be transitioned to a buprenorphine formulation that allows for dose adjustments. 2. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of buspirone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, cobicistat also increases buspirone levels or effects via the same mechanism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. A reduced dose of buspirone may be necessary. 3. Butalbital decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution should be exercised, and monitoring is recommended. 4. Cobicistat and calcifediol interact by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. CYP450 inhibitors may inhibit enzymes involved in vitamin D metabolism (CYP24A1 and CYP27B1), potentially altering serum calcifediol levels and reducing its conversion to calcitriol. Dose adjustments of calcifediol may be required, and serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D, intact PTH, and calcium concentrations should be closely monitored when initiating or discontinuing a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 5. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of cannabidiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, cobicistat increases cannabidiol levels or effects via the same mechanism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when coadministered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 6. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of capmatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution should be exercised, and monitoring is recommended. 7. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of carbamazepine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, cobicistat increases carbamazepine levels or effects via the same mechanism. Plasma levels should be monitored when used concomitantly. 8. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of cariprazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors requires cariprazine dose reduction. Refer to the drug monograph for dosage modification details. 9. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of carvedilol by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution should be exercised, and monitoring is recommended. 10. Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat and darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Increase the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as needed when coadministered with cenobamate. 11. Darunavir increases the levels of ceritinib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution should be exercised, and monitoring is recommended. 12. Cobicistat and darunavir increase the levels or effects of chlordiazepoxide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Consider lowering the benzodiazepine dose. 13. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ciclesonide (inhaled) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, cobicistat increases ciclesonide levels or effects via the same mechanism. Caution should be exercised, and monitoring is recommended. 14. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of cilostazol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the cilostazol dose to 50 mg twice daily when coadministered, and monitor for cilostazol-related adverse effects. 15. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of cinacalcet by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution should be exercised, and monitoring is recommended. 16. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of citalopram by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, darunavir increases citalopram levels or effects via the same mechanism. Coadministration with SSRIs, TCAs, or trazodone may require dose titration of the antidepressant to achieve the desired effect. Monitor for antidepressant response. 17. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Consider alternative antibiotics if clarithromycin is coadministered with darunavir (plus ritonavir or cobicistat). 18. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of clomipramine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Similarly, darunavir increases clomipramine levels or effects via CYP3A4 inhibition. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to the desired effect, using the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose, and monitor for antidepressant response. 19. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of clonazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical monitoring is recommended upon coadministration with anticonvulsants. 20. Darunavir decreases the levels or effects of clopidogrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing clopidogrel bioactivation. Caution should be exercised, and monitoring is recommended. 21. Cobicistat and darunavir increase the levels or effects of clorazepate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Adjust the clorazepate dose if necessary. 22. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of clozapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution should be exercised, and monitoring is recommended. 23. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of colchicine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with colchicine is contraindicated in patients with renal and/or hepatic impairment due to the potential for serious and/or life-threatening reactions. Dosage adjustment of colchicine may be necessary upon coadministration with cobicistat. 24. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens (vaginal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution should be exercised, and monitoring is recommended. 25. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of cortisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while cortisone decreases the levels or effects of darunavir via the same mechanism. Caution should be exercised, and monitoring is recommended. 26. Darunavir increases the levels of crizotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Crizotinib also increases darunavir levels via the same mechanism. Dose reduction may be needed for coadministered drugs predominantly metabolized by CYP3A. 27. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of cyclophosphamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution should be exercised, and monitoring is recommended. 28. Cyclosporine increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, darunavir and cobicistat increase cyclosporine levels or effects via the same mechanism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 29. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of dabigatran by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration of dabigatran with P-gp inhibitors if CrCl <30 mL/min for atrial fibrillation or <50 mL/min for DVT/PE treatment. 30. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 31. Danazol increases the levels or effects of cobicistat and darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution should be exercised, and monitoring is recommended. 32. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dapsone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution should be exercised, and monitoring is recommended. 33. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of darifenacin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, darifenacin increases darunavir levels via the same mechanism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 34. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of darolutamide by inhibiting P-gp and CYP3A4 metabolism. Closely monitor for increased adverse reactions and modify the darolutamide dose as needed. 35. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of dasatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dosage adjustment of dasatinib may be necessary upon coadministration. 36. Deferasirox decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution should be exercised, and monitoring is recommended. 37. Cobicistat and darunavir increase the levels or effects of deflazacort by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Decrease the deflazacort dose to one-third of the recommended dose if coadministered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 38. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of desipramine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to the desired effect, using the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose, and monitor for antidepressant response. 39. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of desvenlafaxine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution should be exercised, and monitoring is recommended. 40. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of deutetrabenazine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Do not exceed 18 mg/dose and 36 mg/day of deutetrabenazine if coadministered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. 41. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of dexamethasone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while dexamethasone decreases darunavir levels via the same mechanism. Caution should be exercised, and monitoring is recommended. 42. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution should be exercised, and monitoring is recommended. 43. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of dextroamphetamine (transdermal) by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution should be exercised, and monitoring is recommended.
